Replace each `___` with code, remove `#| eval: false` and run the chunk. Write your answer under each chunk.

The penguins come with the palmerpenguins package. Put `rosling_tidy.csv` in the `data` folder of the project.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse, palmerpenguins)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
rosling_tidy <- read_csv(here("data", "rosling_tidy.csv"))
```

## 0. One number for the whole table

The mean of a column with missing values is `NA`.

```{r}
#| label: na-example
penguins |>
  summarize(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g))
```

`na.rm = TRUE` removes the missing values before the mean.

```{r}
#| label: na-rm-example
penguins |>
  summarize(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE))
```

### Your turn 0

Compute the mean flipper length of all penguins.

```{r}
#| label: turn-0
#| eval: false
penguins |>
  summarize(mean_flipper = mean(flipper_length_mm, ___ = TRUE))
```

Answer: [YOUR ANSWER HERE] mm.

## 1. Split, apply, combine

`group_by()` splits the rows, `mean()` applies, `summarize()` combines.

```{r}
#| label: group-example
penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarize(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE))
```

### Your turn 1

Compute the mean flipper length of each species.

```{r}
#| label: turn-1
#| eval: false
penguins |>
  group_by(___) |>
  summarize(mean_flipper = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE))
```

Answer: [YOUR ANSWER HERE] has the longest flippers.

## 2. Rows behind each mean

`n()` counts the rows of each group.

```{r}
#| label: n-example
penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarize(n = n(), mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE))
```

`count()` splits and counts in one step. With two variables it gives one row for each combination.

```{r}
#| label: count-example
penguins |>
  count(species, island)
```

For each island, count the penguins and compute the mean bill length.

```{r}
#| label: turn-2
#| eval: false
penguins |>
  group_by(island) |>
  summarize(n = ___, mean_bill = mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE))
```

Answer: [YOUR ANSWER HERE] has the shortest bills.

## 3. Combine the verbs

Females only, the mean mass of each species, from the heaviest to the lightest.

```{r}
#| label: combine-example
penguins |>
  filter(sex == "female") |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarize(n = n(), mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_mass))
```


## 4. Gapminder: a mean of countries or of people?

Look at the data first. One row for each country and year.

```{r}
#| label: look-rosling
rosling_tidy |>
  glimpse()
```

`mean()` gives each country one vote.

```{r}
#| label: mean-asia
rosling_tidy |>
  filter(year == 2007, continent == "Asia") |>
  summarize(mean_life = mean(life_exp))
```

The countries behind the mean: China has 1,318,683,096 people and Bahrain has 708,573.

```{r}
#| label: countries-asia
rosling_tidy |>
  filter(year == 2007, continent == "Asia") |>
  arrange(desc(population)) |>
  head(3)
```

To count each person once, multiply each life expectancy by the population, add them up and divide by the total population.

```{r}
#| label: by-hand
rosling_tidy |>
  filter(year == 2007, continent == "Asia") |>
  summarize(mean_life_people = sum(life_exp * population) / sum(population))
```

`weighted.mean()` gives the same result. Give the values first, then the weights.

```{r}
#| label: weighted-mean
rosling_tidy |>
  filter(year == 2007, continent == "Asia") |>
  summarize(mean_life_people = weighted.mean(life_exp, population))
```
